A new extractor that gets this wrong corrupts every metric silently. Assert the record shape directly in the extractor's own unit test, not only through analyze_builtin.

REMEDIATION slice for the four actionable findings of the Phase 5 integration review. Nothing here is at or above the blocking bar; this slice exists because two of them are measurably FALSE claims in prose this run is shipping, and this run's standard is that the direction of any observable change is named honestly.

F1 - COMPLETE THE TAB FIX SO IT SURVIVES LITERAL-MASKING (the substantive one).
_cognitive_approx's python arm reads MASKED lines (_function_metrics passes scan_body) while _nesting_depth_python reads RAW. _token_mask_spans starts its sentinel fill at `len(line) - len(line.lstrip(' '))`, which is 0 on a tab-indented row, so leading TABS are overwritten with the sentinel and s3's new tab-expanding width never sees them. Before s3 this was measurement-neutral because the reader also used lstrip(' '); s3 changed the reader, so it is neutral no longer. MEASURED by the reviewer on byte-identical bodies: raw '\t\t\t\"\"\" if a else \"z\"' masks to 'xxxxxx if a else xxx', raw width 12 versus masked width 0; head scores cognitive 6 for the tab body and 9 for the space body. NOT a regression - base scored 3 - but the fix is incomplete in the UNDER-COUNT direction, which is the direction this codebase forbids. Fix it by EITHER masking continuation rows from the row's full leading-whitespace width (consistent with _py_indent_width) OR having _cognitive_approx take its indent from the RAW line and its hits from the masked line. Then correct the docstring near quality_gate.py:588-590, which still asserts the sentinel fill never erases leading whitespace a nesting reader derives - an invariant s3 made false. Add a tab-indented multi-line-string fixture to TestTabIndentedPython; none of its current fixtures contain a string literal, which is why nothing caught this.

F2 - CORRECT TWO FALSE SHIPPED CLAIMS in CHANGELOG.md. (a) The s3 bullet's bolded claim that a tab-indented file 'measures the same as the identical space-indented file' is refuted by F1's 6-versus-9 measurement; qualify it. (b) The residual paragraph states that lstrip(' ') in the mask helper 'is left as-is on purpose: it picks a raw column index, not a width' - that argues the helper is irrelevant when it is exactly the mechanism that defeats the fix. Replace it with the real residual. A release note that names the one residual and then dismisses it for the wrong reason is worse than not naming it.

F3 - PIN THE DOWNWARD DIRECTION WITH A TEST. The CHANGELOG openly documents that s3 can move results DOWN, and NO fixture pins it: all four TestTabIndentedPython fixtures indent header and body consistently, so all four move up. The reviewer reproduced the down case on valid python - a class with a tab-indented `def` header and an 8-space body - scoring base cognitive 18 / nesting 6 versus head cognitive 14 / nesting 5, which crosses the cognitive threshold of 15 and turns a FAIL into a PASS. Add a module-level mixed-indent fixture pinning the exact post-change numbers, with the measured before/after in the leading comment.

F4 - COLLAPSE THE DUPLICATED ENCLOSURE BOUND. _phantom_has_more_params re-derives `fn['start'] <= line_no < fn['end']` inside a bare `next(...)`, duplicating _strictly_encloses_line. If the two bounds ever drift, next() raises StopIteration, and there is no try/except between analyze_builtin and measure()'s file loop, so it would abort the gate for EVERY file rather than one. Replace both with a single helper returning the record or None, resolved once in _cbrace_name_at and passed down, which also retires the stringly-keyed `state` bag that exists only to keep _looks_like_call_or_control at four parameters. PRESERVE BEHAVIOUR EXACTLY: the reviewer verified next() currently selects the OUTERMOST enclosing record, not the innermost, and that this is safe because whichever record it picks encloses the phantom and is always emitted alongside. Keep that selection identical unless a test proves otherwise.
